newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Transport Council backs idea of rail-freight freeways.
newsitem.headline: Transport Council backs idea of rail-freight freeways.

text.p: The Transport Council agreed on Thursday on guidelines to set up trans-European rail-freight "freeways" to try to halt the sector's steep losses to road hauliers.
But the ministers stopped short of identifying specific routes criss-crossing the EU, a European Commission spokesman told reporters.
"We agreed on the main standards. The next step is to identify the freeways," the spokesman said.

The Commission's railways White Paper of last July, COM(96)421 painted a bleak picture for the future of rail freight, which it said fell from a share of more than 31 percent of the present EU countries' markets in 1970 to just under 15 percent in 1994.
By contrast, the amount of freight moved by road increased from a near 49-percent share in 1970 to more than 71 percent in 1994.

The principles agreed covered access to the freeways, a so-called one-stop-shop for prices, fewer border delays and performance standards. One element would be a possiblity for higher, premium tariffs on designated high-speed lines.
"The situation at the moment is such that freight travels at 16 kilometres (10 miles) per hour because of delays," the spokesman said.

He added that, while the guidelines raised no problems, several countries including Belgium, France, Luxembourg, Portugal and Spain remained concerned about the Commission's other ideas on liberalising the sector.
